The revised `getResult` comment (lines 309-321) now states a second, larger difference: the arm can win with the queue OPEN and EMPTY and return `error.Closed`, where `wait()` would have blocked. The `signal` field doc (lines 84-86) makes the same stale claim: \"The future protocol depends on the strict reading of a wake: a completion is takeable, or the queue is drained.\" The new comment says exactly that reading no longer holds. Consequence: a reader of the public doc writes the obvious `error.Closed => break` (the shape the dispatcher example at lines 41-48 teaches for `wait`) on a select arm, and tears the queue down on a stale wake while operations are still in flight. Those completions are then never taken, which is the leak `isDrained` was added to prevent. The requirement to disambiguate with `isDrained()` lives only in an internal comment on a private-looking site; it belongs in the module doc that describes the select protocol, and the `signal` field doc must stop asserting the strict reading."}, {"file": "src/completion_queue.zig", "line": 392, "severity": "minor", "category": "tests", "title": "New public `isDrained` has no test, and neither documented `false` case is pinned", "body": "`isDrained` is new public API and nothing in the tree calls it, including the tests. The file otherwise pins each queue behavior with a dedicated test, and the two states the predicate exists to separate are already reachable in existing tests: \"select on a drained queue reports error.Closed\" (line 1222) builds the `true` state, and \"close over an in-flight operation does not wake a parked select\" (line 1246) builds the closed-but-not-drained state. Neither asserts the predicate. So the term that carries the whole point of the change, `self.pending.isEmpty()`, is unprotected: dropping it (reducing `isDrained` to `isClosed`) makes a select driver stop while in-flight completions are still coming, and the full suite stays green. Add assertions on both states, plus the open-and-empty case where `false` means \"stale wake, keep driving\"."}]}
